title.narrative: UNDP Bemyndigade partnerskap för hållbar återhämtning 2022-2026
UNDP Empowered Partnerships for Sustainable Recovery 2022-2026

description.narrative: Projektet svarar mot Ukrainas nuvarande krigspåverkade sammanhang och strävar efter att stärka lokala förmågor för att effektivt integrera hållbara utvecklingslösningar i krishantering och ytterligare återhämtningsplanering, genomförande av lokala initiativ för att förbättra ekonomiska möjligheter för krigsdrabbade befolkningar och tillhandahållande av offentliga tjänster, som samt använda den utmaningsdrivna partnerskapsstrategin som framgångsrikt implementerades för att ta itu med sociala och ekonomiska utvecklingsfrågor som lokala samhällen i Ukraina ställts inför under de föregående åren. Det bygger på erfarenheterna från projektet "Empowered Partnership for Sustainable Development" (2018-2022), finansierat av SIDA och implementerat av UNDP. En av de viktigaste utmaningarna som det krigsdrabbade landet för närvarande står inför relaterar främst till de sociala och ekonomiska konsekvenserna av en massiv utvandring av befolkningen till de västra regionerna i Ukraina, såväl som avstängning eller betydande avmattning av företag. verksamhet och därmed ett stort antal arbetslösa kvinnor och män. Viktiga utmaningar står också inför när lokala myndigheter måste klara av att ta emot ett stort antal människor från olika grupper, för att tillgodose deras bostadsbehov och säkerställa deras tillgång till offentliga tjänster.

The project responds to Ukraine’s current war-impacted context and aspires to strengthen local capabilities to effectively integrate sustainable development solutions in crisis response and further recovery planning, implementation of local initiatives for improving economic opportunities for war-affected populations, and public service provisioning, as well as employ the challenge-driven partnership approach that was successfully implemented to address social and economic development issues faced by local communities across Ukraine in the previous years. It builds upon the experience gained within the “Empowered Partnership for Sustainable Development” project (2018-2022), financed by SIDA and implemented by UNDP. One of key challenges currently faced by the war-affected country relate, principally, to the social and economic consequences of a massive exodus of the population towards the western regions of Ukraine, as well as shut-down or significant slow-down of enterprises’ operations and, hence, a large number of jobless women and men. Important challenges are also faced by local authorities having to cope with the hosting of large numbers of people of diverse groups, to meet their housing needs, and ensure their access to public services.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

title.narrative: Financing Agreement between Sweden, represented by SIDA and UNDP

description.narrative:
During 2023, the Project achieved a few positive milestones. The first phase of a tailored Capacity Development Programme was launched, benefiting 335 representatives from local and regional authorities. These participants gained vital skills in effective crisis response, recovery, and public administrative services. Training participants demonstrated the practical application of their newfound knowledge, resulting in tangible outcomes.
A Call for project ideas supported by an information campaign in all targeted regions resulted in 1,265 applications. The Project team has analysed the submitted project ideas and classified the initiatives, based on their level of readiness for implementation and the support required, including for further formulation of implementation-ready project proposals. It is proposed that short-listed projects can benefit from the potential UNDP support by procurement and transfer of highly needed equipment for the provision of public services and for the creation of economic opportunities.
The Open call helped identify 54 potential partnerships, offering support in their development that resulted in the formation of 23 challenge-driven cross-sectoral partnerships which are ready to implement the local initiatives. The Capacity Development Programme was offered to the short-listed project ideas teams.
